As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 104: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 106: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 108: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

![Image 110: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

The American Kennel Club has recognized 202 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 104: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 106: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 108: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

![Image 110: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

The American Kennel Club has recognized 202 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

    4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
    5.   Dachshund

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 104: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 106: Danish-Swedish Farmdog standing in a field of grasses and flowers.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Danish-Swedish-Farmdog-standing-in-a-field-of-grasses-and-flowers.jpg)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 108: Saluki standing on a hill outdoors.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Saluki-standing-on-a-hill-outdoors.jpg)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

AKC is a participant in affiliate advertising programs designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to akc.org. If you purchase a product through this article, we may receive a portion of the sale.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

![Image 110: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/English-Foxhound-standing-in-a-field.jpg)

Chris Strickland/Getty Images Plus via Getty Images

The American Kennel Club has recognized 202 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 104: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 106: Danish-Swedish Farmdog standing in a field of grasses and flowers.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Danish-Swedish-Farmdog-standing-in-a-field-of-grasses-and-flowers.jpg)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 108: Saluki standing on a hill outdoors.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Saluki-standing-on-a-hill-outdoors.jpg)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

![Image 110: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/English-Foxhound-standing-in-a-field.jpg)

Chris Strickland/Getty Images Plus via Getty Images

The American Kennel Club has recognized 202 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

# The Most Popular Dog Breeds of 2023

By [Melanie Haid](https://www.akc.org/author/mxhakc-org/)

 Updated: Apr 09, 2024 | 4 Minutes 

 Updated: Apr 09, 2024 | 4 Minutes 

![Image 102: French Bulldog puppy sitting on the floor in the living room.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/French-Bulldog-puppy-sitting-on-the-floor-in-the-living-room.jpg)

©Olesya - stock.adobe.com

*   [labrador retriever](https://www.akc.org/tag/labrador-retriever/)
*   [french bulldog](https://www.akc.org/tag/french-bulldog/)
*   [most popular breeds](https://www.akc.org/tag/most-popular-breeds/)

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in! Which breed has been named the American Kennel Club’s most popular dog breed of 2023?

For the second year in a row, the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No.1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States! Before 2022, the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) had a firm hold on the top spot, keeping an impressive [31-year reign.](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/)

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

The French Bulldog’s popularity shows no signs of slowing down. You’ve likely seen these bat-eared companions before, and they’re especially popular in cities. Over the last 11 years, the French Bulldog has steadily grown in registration rankings, ranking No. 14 in 2012. In 2021, Frenchies made it to the No. 2 spot, taking over the [top spot officially in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/).

![Image 103](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/non-sporting-group-french-bulldog-winston-surfman.png)

Surfman for WKC

French Bulldog “Winston” won first place in the Non-Sporting Group, moving on to Best in Show at the 2022 AKC National Championship. Winston went on to win Best in Show.

Part of the French Bulldog’s appeal is their playful, smart, and adaptable nature. They’re easy to bring anywhere, and great companions for a variety of lifestyles. These smart little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is one with many layers. Even in the past, they belonged to all kinds of people, from royalty to middle-class artisans. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, giving them over 100 years of AKC history along with it.

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2023

It’s no surprise to dog lovers that the Frenchie remains in the No. 1 spot, and the rest of the top five breeds follow a similar pattern. Same as 2022, the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) are ranked No. 2-5 respectively.

There’s some shuffling in the top 10 from 2022 to 2023. The [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) is making moves, jumping from the No. 9 spot in 2022 to the No. 6 spot in 2023. [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) took their spot at No. 9 in 2023, moving down from No. 7 in 2022.[Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) went from No. 6 in 2022 to No. 7 in 2023. The [Beagle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) remains at No. 8, and the [German Shorthaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remains at No. 10 with no change in rank.

![Image 105: Beagle head portrait in a field in early morning.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Beagle-head-portrait-in-a-field-in-early-morning.jpg)

 ©Dogs - stock.adobe.com

The top 10 breeds aren’t the only ones getting people’s attention. Other breeds working their way up the rank in 2023 were the [Papillion](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/papillon/), the [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/), the [Basenji](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basenji/), and the [Finnish Lapphund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-lapphund/). From 2022 to 2023, the Finnish Lapphund went from No. 167 to No. 135, a total of 32 spots. The Basenji jumped 10 spots from No. 91 to No. 81, and the The Papillion went up six ranks from No. 51 t0 No. 45. The Great Pyrenees went up five spots from 2022 to 2023, going from No. 69 to No. 64.

Over the last decade, breeds like the [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/), [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/), [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), and [English Cocker Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-cocker-spaniel/) have also seen jumps in popularity. The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [Russian Toy](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-toy/), and [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/) were recognized in 2022, but since the Bracco Italiano was recognized in July of that year, they debuted in the registration lists in 2023, at No. 152. The Mudi went from its debut at No. 150 in 2022 to No. 130 in 2023, while the Russian Toy debuted at No. 144 and now ranks No. 141.

The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) was the [newest breed recognized by the AKC](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) starting January 2024. Tune in next year to see where they debut in the ranks!

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2023

Ranked in the bottom five of the 200 breeds were the [Azawakh](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/azawakh/) (No. 196), the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) (No. 197), [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/) (No. 198), [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) (No. 199), and [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/) (No. 200). In 2021, the Norwegian Lundehund took the bottom spot, and has been making its way slowly up the rankings, passing the English Foxhound and Sloughi in 2023.

The American Kennel Club has recognized 201 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

![Image 107: slowmotiongli/Getty Images Plus](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Norwegian-Lundehund-standing-in-profile-outdoors.jpg)

slowmotiongli/Getty Images Plus

The Norwegian Lundehund, recognized in 2011, was ranked No. 198 in the 2023 breed rankings.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation. The AKC and its affiliates have also [donated over $67 million to canine health research](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-82.html) as of 2023, and the [Canine Health Foundation published their 1000th scientific publication](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-79.html) in 2023.

# The Most Popular Dog Breeds of 2023

By [Melanie Haid](https://www.akc.org/author/mxhakc-org/)

 Updated: Apr 09, 2024 | 4 Minutes 

 Updated: Apr 09, 2024 | 4 Minutes 

![Image 102: French Bulldog puppy sitting on the floor in the living room.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/French-Bulldog-puppy-sitting-on-the-floor-in-the-living-room.jpg)

©Olesya - stock.adobe.com

*   [labrador retriever](https://www.akc.org/tag/labrador-retriever/)
*   [french bulldog](https://www.akc.org/tag/french-bulldog/)
*   [most popular breeds](https://www.akc.org/tag/most-popular-breeds/)

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in! Which breed has been named the American Kennel Club’s most popular dog breed of 2023?

For the second year in a row, the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No.1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States! Before 2022, the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) had a firm hold on the top spot, keeping an impressive [31-year reign.](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/)

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

The French Bulldog’s popularity shows no signs of slowing down. You’ve likely seen these bat-eared companions before, and they’re especially popular in cities. Over the last 11 years, the French Bulldog has steadily grown in registration rankings, ranking No. 14 in 2012. In 2021, Frenchies made it to the No. 2 spot, taking over the [top spot officially in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/).

![Image 103](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/non-sporting-group-french-bulldog-winston-surfman.png)

Surfman for WKC

French Bulldog “Winston” won first place in the Non-Sporting Group, moving on to Best in Show at the 2022 AKC National Championship. Winston went on to win Best in Show.

Part of the French Bulldog’s appeal is their playful, smart, and adaptable nature. They’re easy to bring anywhere, and great companions for a variety of lifestyles. These smart little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is one with many layers. Even in the past, they belonged to all kinds of people, from royalty to middle-class artisans. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, giving them over 100 years of AKC history along with it.

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2023

It’s no surprise to dog lovers that the Frenchie remains in the No. 1 spot, and the rest of the top five breeds follow a similar pattern. Same as 2022, the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) are ranked No. 2-5 respectively.

There’s some shuffling in the top 10 from 2022 to 2023. The [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) is making moves, jumping from the No. 9 spot in 2022 to the No. 6 spot in 2023. [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) took their spot at No. 9 in 2023, moving down from No. 7 in 2022.[Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) went from No. 6 in 2022 to No. 7 in 2023. The [Beagle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) remains at No. 8, and the [German Shorthaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remains at No. 10 with no change in rank.

![Image 105: Beagle head portrait in a field in early morning.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Beagle-head-portrait-in-a-field-in-early-morning.jpg)

 ©Dogs - stock.adobe.com

The top 10 breeds aren’t the only ones getting people’s attention. Other breeds working their way up the rank in 2023 were the [Papillion](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/papillon/), the [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/), the [Basenji](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basenji/), and the [Finnish Lapphund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-lapphund/). From 2022 to 2023, the Finnish Lapphund went from No. 167 to No. 135, a total of 32 spots. The Basenji jumped 10 spots from No. 91 to No. 81, and the The Papillion went up six ranks from No. 51 t0 No. 45. The Great Pyrenees went up five spots from 2022 to 2023, going from No. 69 to No. 64.

Over the last decade, breeds like the [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/), [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/), [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), and [English Cocker Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-cocker-spaniel/) have also seen jumps in popularity. The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [Russian Toy](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-toy/), and [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/) were recognized in 2022, but since the Bracco Italiano was recognized in July of that year, they debuted in the registration lists in 2023, at No. 152. The Mudi went from its debut at No. 150 in 2022 to No. 130 in 2023, while the Russian Toy debuted at No. 144 and now ranks No. 141.

The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) was the [newest breed recognized by the AKC](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) starting January 2024. Tune in next year to see where they debut in the ranks!

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2023

Ranked in the bottom five of the 200 breeds were the [Azawakh](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/azawakh/) (No. 196), the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) (No. 197), [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/) (No. 198), [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) (No. 199), and [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/) (No. 200). In 2021, the Norwegian Lundehund took the bottom spot, and has been making its way slowly up the rankings, passing the English Foxhound and Sloughi in 2023.

The American Kennel Club has recognized 201 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

![Image 107: slowmotiongli/Getty Images Plus](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Norwegian-Lundehund-standing-in-profile-outdoors.jpg)

slowmotiongli/Getty Images Plus

The Norwegian Lundehund, recognized in 2011, was ranked No. 198 in the 2023 breed rankings.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation. The AKC and its affiliates have also [donated over $67 million to canine health research](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-82.html) as of 2023, and the [Canine Health Foundation published their 1000th scientific publication](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-79.html) in 2023.

The numbers are in! Which breed will be named the American Kennel Club’s most popular dog breed of 2022? As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year.

And for the first time in history, 2022 found the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) taking the No. 1 spot. This ends the [Labrador Retriever’s](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)[31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) as the most popular dog breed in America.

## The New Top Dog

The French Bulldog has moved into the number one position after climbing the ranks in popularity over the last ten years. In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked at No. 14. Since then, registrations have increased by over 1,000%, bringing this playful breed to the top. French Bulldogs held the No. 2 spot in 2021.

Breaking the Lab’s top-dog status of over three decades is no small feat. The Frenchie is a smart, compact breed, and they can fit into various different lifestyles, perfect for people all across the country. This petite dog was first recognized by the AKC in 1898; they are beloved by everyone from families to single owners for their charming and adaptable nature. They have surged in popularity in cities across the country since their small size and generally quiet demeanor make them good fits for apartments and smaller homes.

![Image 104: French Bulldog puppy head portrait outdoors.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/French-Bulldog-puppy-head-portrait-outdoors.jpeg)

©Sporthorse Photography - stock.adobe.com

The French Bulldog takes the number one spot after the Labrador Retriever’s 31-year run

## Top Five Dog Breeds of 2022

Aside from this massive move, the top five list looks a bit familiar. The Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) take ranks two through five, respectively. [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) moved from No. 8 to No. 7, while the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) bumped the [German Shorthaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) from No. 9 in 2021 to No. 10 in 2022.

Other breeds that made major jumps from 2021 to 2022 are the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), [Gordon Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/gordon-setter/), [Italian Greyhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/italian-greyhound/), and [Anatolian Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/anatolian-shepherd-dog/). Over the last ten years, breeds like the [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/), [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/), [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), and [English Cocker Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-cocker-spaniel/) have been making their way up the rankings in popularity, as well.

[Newly recognized](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/) by the AKC [in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/russian-toy-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-breed-in-2022/), the [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/) and [Russian Toy](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-toy/) debuted at No. 150 and No. 144—not bad for their first year! The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/) became the [200th breed fully recognized by the AK](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/)[C](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/)in July of 2022; as a result, it will debut in the registration rankings for 2023.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2022

At the bottom of the list (Nos. 197 through 199) are the [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/), and [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/). Last year, the Norwegian Lundehund was at the bottom, but they have surpassed English Foxhounds in registration over the past year. English Foxhounds, like their [American Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-foxhound/) cousins, were bred as agile, scent-driven hunting dogs.

The American Kennel Club, which was founded in 1884, recognizes 200 breeds, with additional breeds working their way toward recognition comprising the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration; the AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation. The [AKC and its affiliates have also donated over $67 million to canine health research](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-74.html) as of 2022, and donated its 100 th AKC Pet Disaster Relief Trailer in November of 2022.

The numbers are in! Which breed will be named the American Kennel Club’s most popular dog breed of 2022? As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year.

And for the first time in history, 2022 found the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) taking the No. 1 spot. This ends the [Labrador Retriever’s](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)[31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) as the most popular dog breed in America.

## The New Top Dog

The French Bulldog has moved into the number one position after climbing the ranks in popularity over the last ten years. In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked at No. 14. Since then, registrations have increased by over 1,000%, bringing this playful breed to the top. French Bulldogs held the No. 2 spot in 2021.

Breaking the Lab’s top-dog status of over three decades is no small feat. The Frenchie is a smart, compact breed, and they can fit into various different lifestyles, perfect for people all across the country. This petite dog was first recognized by the AKC in 1898; they are beloved by everyone from families to single owners for their charming and adaptable nature. They have surged in popularity in cities across the country since their small size and generally quiet demeanor make them good fits for apartments and smaller homes.

![Image 104: French Bulldog puppy head portrait outdoors.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/French-Bulldog-puppy-head-portrait-outdoors.jpeg)

©Sporthorse Photography - stock.adobe.com

The French Bulldog takes the number one spot after the Labrador Retriever’s 31-year run

## Top Five Dog Breeds of 2022

Aside from this massive move, the top five list looks a bit familiar. The Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) take ranks two through five, respectively. [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) moved from No. 8 to No. 7, while the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) bumped the [German Shorthaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) from No. 9 in 2021 to No. 10 in 2022.

AKC is a participant in affiliate advertising programs designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to akc.org. If you purchase a product through this article, we may receive a portion of the sale.

Other breeds that made major jumps from 2021 to 2022 are the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), [Gordon Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/gordon-setter/), [Italian Greyhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/italian-greyhound/), and [Anatolian Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/anatolian-shepherd-dog/). Over the last ten years, breeds like the [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/), [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/), [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), and [English Cocker Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-cocker-spaniel/) have been making their way up the rankings in popularity, as well.

[Newly recognized](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/) by the AKC [in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/russian-toy-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-breed-in-2022/), the [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/) and [Russian Toy](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-toy/) debuted at No. 150 and No. 144—not bad for their first year! The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/) became the [200th breed fully recognized by the AK](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/)[C](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/)in July of 2022; as a result, it will debut in the registration rankings for 2023.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2022

At the bottom of the list (Nos. 197 through 199) are the [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/), and [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/). Last year, the Norwegian Lundehund was at the bottom, but they have surpassed English Foxhounds in registration over the past year. English Foxhounds, like their [American Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-foxhound/) cousins, were bred as agile, scent-driven hunting dogs.

The American Kennel Club, which was founded in 1884, recognizes 200 breeds, with additional breeds working their way toward recognition comprising the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration; the AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation. The [AKC and its affiliates have also donated over $67 million to canine health research](https://www.akcchf.org/news-events/news/akc-canine-health-foundation-74.html) as of 2022, and donated its 100 th AKC Pet Disaster Relief Trailer in November of 2022.

It goes without saying that in your house, your dog is the most popular. But what do the statistics say? The American Kennel Club has used registration data to compile the list of 2021’s most popular breeds. As always, the [Labrador Retriever](https://retrievist.akc.org/gift-guides/what-you-need-for-a-labrador-retriever/) tops the list — this time for the 31st year! [The Lab’s temperament and versatility are just two of the traits](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/news/americas-record-setting-dog-versatility-temperament/)that contribute to its perennial popularity.

Most notably, the [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) has moved back into the top five for the first time since 1997. In general, most breeds are about [as popular as they were in 2020](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/the-most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2020/), with a few exceptions. The[Field Spaniel,](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/lifestyle/5-reasons-to-love-the-field-spaniel/) for example, moved up 24 places to #136, while the [Puli](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/puli-history-how-the-ancient-hungarian-sheepdog-got-cords/), with its unique corded coat, dropped 21 places to #164. A breed new to the list is the [Biewer Terrier](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/biewer-terrier-akc-recognized-breed-2021/), debuting at #83. The AKC recognized the breed in January, 2021 and the Toy dog has already won hearts and minds.

At the bottom of the list is the intriguing [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund-history-behind-the-breed/), one of the rarest breeds of dogs, which ranks 197 of 197 breeds. The [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/)– literally, “puffin dog” – [would scale sheer-faced cliffs](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund-history-behind-the-breed/) to raid puffin nests, bringing the still-live birds back to their masters.

In a time when there are more [families with dogs than with children](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/lifestyle/great-breeds-first-time-owners/), it’s no surprise that the breeds vary widely, from large guard dogs, to agile herders, to tiny toy breeds and everything in between. Some breeds even increase in [popularity based on TV shows and movies](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/price-of-popularity-breed-trends/). [The pandemic](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeding/early-socialization-puppies-pandemic/) has been an especially favorable time for new dog owners to decide to [bring home a puppy](https://retrievist.akc.org/essentials/bringing-home-a-new-puppy-essentials/).

Using these statistics to compile an annual popularity list is a relatively minor benefit of dog registration. The American Kennel Club is the only purebred dog registry in the United States maintaining systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs throughout the country. Additionally, the American Kennel Club and its affiliates have donated over $38 million to canine health research and $7 million to pet disaster relief.

dragon for real/Moment via Getty Images

The Poodle, which comes in three sizes, ranked in the top five dog breeds for the first time since 1997.

It goes without saying that in your house, your dog is the most popular. But what do the statistics say? The American Kennel Club has used registration data to compile the list of 2021’s most popular breeds. As always, the [Labrador Retriever](https://retrievist.akc.org/gift-guides/what-you-need-for-a-labrador-retriever/) tops the list — this time for the 31st year! [The Lab’s temperament and versatility are just two of the traits](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/news/americas-record-setting-dog-versatility-temperament/)that contribute to its perennial popularity.

Most notably, the [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) has moved back into the top five for the first time since 1997. In general, most breeds are about [as popular as they were in 2020](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/the-most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2020/), with a few exceptions. The[Field Spaniel,](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/lifestyle/5-reasons-to-love-the-field-spaniel/) for example, moved up 24 places to #136, while the [Puli](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/puli-history-how-the-ancient-hungarian-sheepdog-got-cords/), with its unique corded coat, dropped 21 places to #164. A breed new to the list is the [Biewer Terrier](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/biewer-terrier-akc-recognized-breed-2021/), debuting at #83. The AKC recognized the breed in January, 2021 and the Toy dog has already won hearts and minds.

At the bottom of the list is the intriguing [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund-history-behind-the-breed/), one of the rarest breeds of dogs, which ranks 197 of 197 breeds. The [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund/)– literally, “puffin dog” – [would scale sheer-faced cliffs](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/norwegian-lundehund-history-behind-the-breed/) to raid puffin nests, bringing the still-live birds back to their masters.

In a time when there are more [families with dogs than with children](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/lifestyle/great-breeds-first-time-owners/), it’s no surprise that the breeds vary widely, from large guard dogs, to agile herders, to tiny toy breeds and everything in between. Some breeds even increase in [popularity based on TV shows and movies](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/price-of-popularity-breed-trends/). [The pandemic](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeding/early-socialization-puppies-pandemic/) has been an especially favorable time for new dog owners to decide to [bring home a puppy](https://retrievist.akc.org/essentials/bringing-home-a-new-puppy-essentials/).

Using these statistics to compile an annual popularity list is a relatively minor benefit of dog registration. The American Kennel Club is the only purebred dog registry in the United States maintaining systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs throughout the country. Additionally, the American Kennel Club and its affiliates have donated over $38 million to canine health research and $7 million to pet disaster relief.

The Poodle, which comes in three sizes, ranked in the top five dog breeds for the first time since 1997.

# The Most Popular Dog Breeds of 2020

By [Jan Reisen](https://www.akc.org/author/jan-reisen/)

 Updated: May 30, 2023 | 3 Minutes 

 Updated: May 30, 2023 | 3 Minutes 

![Image 102: Labrador retriever puppies sleeping side by side in the grass.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Labrador-retriever-puppies-sleeping-side-by-side-in-the-grass.jpeg)

©Chatchai.b - stock.adobe.com

*   [most popular breeds](https://www.akc.org/tag/most-popular-breeds/)

_For the most updated statistics, check out the latest rankings of America’s most popular dog breeds._

Is your dog’s breed winning popularity contests this year? Now you can find out! The most popular dog breeds of 2020 were released on March 16, 2021, based on American Kennel Club registration statistics.

America continues its love affair with the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) which tops the list for the 30 th year in a row. Just below the Lab, the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the #2 spot, ranking above the [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/) and [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/) for the first time. And the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) makes its way into the top 10 this year, knocking the [Pembroke Welsh Corgi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pembroke-welsh-corgi/) down to #11.

Some breeds rose in popularity, including the [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/), which jumped from 60 th in 2014 to 37 th this year. Some breeds declined in popularity, like the [Coton de Tulear](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/coton-de-tulear/), which dropped 50 spots from 31 to 81, and the [Boerbel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boerboel/), which declined almost 60 spots.

Like clothing styles and baby names, [dog breeds](https://chewy.sjv.io/Xmeem5) go in and out of style. It’s likely that pop culture plays a large role in preferences. In fact, a [study](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/09/140910152512.htm) from the University of Bristol, City University of New York, and Western Carolina University found that movies, specifically durably popular ones, play a large role in breed popularity. For most of the 20th century, a breed’s temperament, health, and longevity played less of a role in selecting a dog than its association with a popular film.

The study used registration statistics from the AKC to compile and analyze the data. But there are more substantial reasons that [dog registration is important](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/advice/why-register-your-dog-with-the-akc/).The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States, maintaining systematic investigations and inspections. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the safety, welfare, and health of dogs throughout the country.Additionally, the American Kennel Club and its affiliates have donated over $38 million to canine health research and $7 million to pet disaster relief.
